Head_and_Face: Beak is small, curved, and orange-red.
Eyes are orange-red to brown.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is compact.
Plumage varies by species but typically includes vivid combinations of red, green, blue, and yellow.
Common pattern is red head and breast with green wings and back, or green body with red, blue, and yellow accents.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are grey with zygodactyl feet (two toes forward, two backward) adapted for climbing.
Wings are short and rounded.
Tail is moderately long and graduated.

Head_and_Face: Beak is stout, slightly curved, and dark.
Eyes are red to orange-red.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust and crow-like.
Plumage is typically black, chestnut, or brown depending on species.
Common pattern is glossy black body with chestnut wings.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Most distinctive feature is the elongated, dagger-like hind claw on each foot, disproportionately long and straight.
Legs are strong and adapted for walking on the ground.
Wings are broad and rounded, adapted for short flights.
Tail is long and graduated.

Head_and_Face: Most distinctive feature is the long, slender, decurved (downward-curving) black beak.
Eyes are dark red to brown with a black eye-stripe.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is slender.
Plumage typically includes vivid combinations of green, blue, yellow, and red.
Common pattern is green back and wings with yellow throat, blue breast, and red-brown crown.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are small and weak with syndactyl feet (three forward toes partially fused).
Wings are long and pointed, adapted for agile, graceful flight.
Tail is elongated with central feathers extended into streamers in many species.

Head_and_Face: Most distinctive feature is the enormous casque (bony protuberance) on top of the massive bill.
Bill is massive, laterally compressed, and brightly colored (yellow, orange, or red) with a curved tip.
Eyes are red, yellow, or brown with a dark eye-stripe.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust.
Plumage is typically black, white, or brown with contrasting wing and tail patterns.
Common pattern is black body with white belly and tail band.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are short and stout with zygodactyl feet (two toes forward, two backward).
Wings are broad and rounded.
Tail is long and graduated.

Head_and_Face: Most distinctive feature is the extremely long, slender bill adapted for feeding on nectar; bill may be straight, decurved, or sickle-shaped.
Eyes are large and dark.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is tiny.
Plumage is brilliantly iridescent with metallic green, red, blue, or purple coloration that shifts with viewing angle.
Iridescence is created by light refraction through feather microstructure.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Wings are short and blade-like, beating 50-80 times per second creating a humming sound.
Legs are tiny and weak with small feet adapted only for perching, not walking.
Tail is short and forked or rounded.

Head_and_Face: Most distinctive feature is the long, straight, pointed bill adapted for catching insects in flight; bill is black or dark grey and sharply pointed.
Eyes are dark with a pale eye-ring.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is slender.
Plumage is metallic green, bronze, or copper with iridescent sheen that shifts with viewing angle.
Underparts are typically rufous, white, or buff.
Plumage is glossy and metallic.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are small and weak with syndactyl feet (three forward toes partially fused).
Wings are long and pointed, adapted for agile flight.
Tail is long and graduated or squared.

Head_and_Face: Most distinctive feature is the enormous, brightly colored bill (up to one-third of body length), laterally compressed, with combinations of yellow, orange, red, green, and blue.
Eyes are surrounded by bare, brightly colored skin (blue, yellow, or orange).
Body_and_Plumage: Body plumage is typically black with contrasting patches of white, red, yellow, or blue on the throat, breast, or tail.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are short and stout with zygodactyl feet (two toes forward, two backward) adapted for climbing.
Wings are short and rounded, adapted for short flights through forest canopy.
Tail is moderately long and squared.

Head_and_Face: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
Eyes are dark.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
Wings are broad and pointed.
Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.

Head_and_Face: Male exhibits dark green iridescent head with shaggy crest.
Most distinctive feature is the long, thin, serrated bill (saw-like edges) adapted for catching fish; bill is red with a black tip and hooked nail.
Eyes are red.
Body_and_Plumage: Male has white neck collar, bright rust-red breast, and grey-black body with white flank patches.
Female is grey-brown with a shaggy reddish-brown head and white throat.
Body is streamlined and buoyant.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet adapted for swimming and diving.
Wings are broad and pointed.
Tail is short and pointed.

Head_and_Face: Most distinctive feature is the long neck (longer than ducks) and the stout, flattened bill with a nail (hard tip) at the end.
Bill is typically orange, pink, or black.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust and stocky, large and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
Plumage varies by species: common patterns include grey-brown with darker barring, white with black wingtips, or black with white cheek patches.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are short and set centrally on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
Wings are broad and powerful, adapted for long migratory flights.
Tail is short and rounded.
